parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Australia's Airborne Dentists
parts.article:
Australia's Airborne Dentists
 
(A) Australians living or travelling in rural and remote areas can face particular difficulties when they need medical care. Hundreds of kilometres from major cities and many hours by road from the closest hospital or clinic, some rural Australians do not have easy access to doctors, nurses and dentists. Organisations such as the Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) have been established to bring health services to outback Australian communities. The RFDS provides free medical care to people who live, work or travel in remote and regional parts of Australia. This non-profit organisation is the oldest and largest airborne health service of its kind in the world, and since 1928 it has used small aircraft to send doctors and nurses to some of Australia's most far-away communities.
 
(B) In recent years, the RFDS has also started to fly dentists to regional Australia. As well as offering mobile dental clinics, the RFDS offers a range of preventative and educational services. Looking after the teeth of people in remote areas presents special challenges. These include providing care to disparate communities with no established dental facilities, and dealing with higher incidences of other diseases which are linked to, or caused by poor dental health.
 
(C) People in remote areas have very infrequent visits by health staff. RFDS dentists might only visit a community once every few months, or sometimes once per year. Because of infrequent dentist visits, patients in these areas often need to put up with their dental problems before they can get treatment. Consequently, people in remote areas are more likely to have tooth decay (the blackening and deterioration of teeth) and develop gum and other mouth diseases.
 
(D) In some locations that the RFDS visits, there are no suitable dental facilities, so dentists have to bring everything with them. This includes drills, dentists' chairs, portable X-ray machines, and computers for keeping track of patients' treatments. Equipment can weigh up to 100 kilograms, and since the small planes that transport dentists have limited space, dentists cannot always bring everything that they need.
 
(E) While dentists in town or city centres can specialise in certain types of treatment, RFDS dentists need to be 'all-rounders'. They need to be able to do all kinds of dental procedures, as they don't have the ability to refer patients to more specialised dentists. Even with their broad experience, there are some services that are particularly challenging for RFDS dentists. For example, dentures (or artificial teeth) can be very difficult to provide, as they need to be the right shape and size for the patient, and this requires many visits over a long period of time. As a result, it is not practical to make dentures available.
 
(F) Some chronic illnesses are more common in remote communities than in the rest of Australia. These illnesses can in turn lead to a lowered resistance to infection, including gum and other oral infections. As a result, people in outback Australian communities are more likely to experience oral health problems than city folk, and this poses extra challenges for both the dentists and the doctors of the RFDS.
 
(G) Because there aren't a lot of dental services in remote areas, people living in these areas also receive less education about good dental hygiene than their city counterparts do. Australians in very remote communities might not be aware of things that people in cities take for granted, such as the importance of daily tooth brushing. Also, basic dental hygiene items such as toothpaste and toothbrushes can be more expensive in outback areas. Many people are on low incomes, meaning they have extra difficulty affording these products. If this is the case, the RFDS supplies these.
 
(H) As well as treating patients, RFDS dentists try to focus on preventative oral health and educate their patients on good oral hygiene, such as tooth brushing and flossing. The RFDS also provides mouthguards for young sports players. Playing contact sports, such as rugby league or Australian rules football, can damage young people's teeth, so mouthguards provide protection which prevents accidental injuries.
 
(I) Adding fluoride to water supplies has been proven to reduce the incidence of tooth decay in many parts of the world. City dwellers in Australia use water supplies that have been fluoridated, and their rates of tooth decay are lower because of this. In remote areas, it is not practical to fluoridate drinking water supplies, and so people living in these areas are more subject to tooth decay. As a result, it is particularly important that people living in areas without fluoridated water pay special attention to regular brushing of their teeth with fluoridated toothpaste.
 
(J) Despite many challenges, the RFDS continues to offer much needed dental and medical support. Its presence in isolated communities greatly improves the quality of dental health, and supports important oral hygiene and health initiatives.

questions.question: Many of the RFDS doctors work as volunteers.

analyses.content: 你可能看到“non-profit”（非营利）或“free medical care”（免费医疗），就想当然地认为医生也是免费干活（volunteer）的，这是两码事。

(Paragraph A) The RFDS provides free medical care to people who live, work or travel in remote and regional parts of Australia. This non-profit organisation is the oldest and largest airborne health service of its kind in the world...
文章只提到了RFDS是一个非营利组织（non-profit organisation），提供免费医疗，但完全没有提到医生本人是不是志愿者（即是否拿工资）。

questions.question: RFDS dentists make trips to outback communities each month.

analyses.content: 文章明确说牙医去偏远地区的频率是“每几个月一次”（once every few months）甚至“一年一次”（once per year），这与题目说的“每个月”（each month）矛盾。
看到时间词要敏感，文中是“every few months”（每隔几个月），千万别看漏了 "few" 把它当成了 "every month"。
(Paragraph C) People in remote areas have very infrequent visits by health staff. RFDS dentists might only visit a community once every few months, or sometimes once per year.

questions.question: RFDS dentists are accompanied on their journeys to remote areas by a dental nurse.

analyses.content: 文章提到飞机空间有限，牙医不能带所有东西，但完全没提他们飞行时是否有“牙科护士”（dental nurse）陪同。
虽然第一段提到了RFDS运送“doctors and nurses”，但这道题问的是专门陪同“dentists”的人，不要把普通护士和牙医助理混为一谈。
(Paragraph D) ...since the small planes that transport dentists have limited space, dentists cannot always bring everything that they need.

questions.question: RFDS dentists must provide a wide range of dental services.

analyses.content: 文章说RFDS的牙医必须是“全能选手”（all-rounders），需要能做“各种各样”（all kinds of）的牙科手术，这与题目中的“wide range”一致。
你要理解 "all-rounders"（多面手/全能）和 "all kinds of procedures" 就是题目中 "wide range of services" 的同义替换。

(Paragraph E) While dentists in town or city centres can specialise in certain types of treatment, RFDS dentists need to be 'all-rounders'. They need to be able to do all kinds of dental procedures, as they don't have the ability to refer patients to more specialised dentists.

questions.question: Rural dental patients are more informed about oral hygiene than urban patients.

analyses.content: 文章明确说偏远地区的人接受的牙齿卫生教育比城市人“更少”（receive less education），而不是“more informed”（更了解）。
只要看到原文中的 "less education" 和题目中的 "more informed" 是反义关系，就可以直接判定为错。
(Paragraph G) Because there aren't a lot of dental services in remote areas, people living in these areas also receive less education about good dental hygiene than their city counterparts do.

questions.question: RFDS dentists educate patients about good eating habits.

analyses.content: (Paragraph H) As well as treating patients, RFDS dentists try to focus on preventative oral health and educate their patients on good oral hygiene, such as tooth brushing and flossing.
文章提到了牙医会教病人“刷牙和使用牙线”（tooth brushing and flossing），但没有提到教病人关于“饮食习惯”（eating habits）的内容。
你可能觉得“保护牙齿”肯定包括“少吃糖”，但这属于你的常识脑补，原文没写“eating habits”就不能选。

questions.question: Urban Australians generally have better teeth because their water is treated.

analyses.content: 文章说城市居民的供水加了氟（fluoridated），因此他们的蛀牙率更低，这与题目说的“水被处理过所以牙更好”一致。
题目中的 "water is treated" 对应原文的 "water supplies that have been fluoridated"（加氟就是一种处理方式）。
(Paragraph I) City dwellers in Australia use water supplies that have been fluoridated, and their rates of tooth decay are lower because of this.

(Paragraph D) ...and since the small planes that transport dentists have limited space, dentists cannot always bring everything that they need.
原文括号里解释了 dentures 就是 "artificial teeth"，但题目限制只能填一个词，所以必须填 "dentures"。
定位到E段中间，文中提到对于RFDS牙医来说，提供 "dentures"（假牙）是非常困难且不切实际的。
(Paragraph E) For example, dentures (or artificial teeth) can be very difficult to provide... As a result, it is not practical to make dentures available.
定位到G段末尾，文中提到如果病人买不起，RFDS会提供 "toothpaste" 和 "toothbrushes"。
